message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – Key Properties

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Symbol** | H |
| **Atomic mass** | ~1.008 u (average of isotopes) |
| **Isotopes** | ¹H (protium), ²H (deuterium), ³H (tritium) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Electronegativity (Pauling)** | 2.20 |
| **First ionization energy** | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ/mol) |
| **Electron affinity** | –0.754 eV (–72.8 kJ/mol) |
| **Boiling point** | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| **Density at STP** | 0.0899 g/L (0.0000899 g/cm³) |
| **Molar volume at STP** | 22.414 L/mol |
| **State at room temperature** | Gas |
| **Bond type** | Covalent (in H₂) |
| **Common oxidation states** | +1 (most compounds), –1 (hydrides) |
| **Acidity/basicity** | Acts as a weak acid (forming hydronium, H₃O⁺) in aqueous solution; forms hydride ions (H⁻) in metal hydrides |
| **Reactivity** | Highly reactive; burns in oxygen to form water (exothermic). Forms hydrides with metals and nonmetals. |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR) – fundamental for astrophysical spectroscopy. |
| **Applications** | Fuel (hydrogen fuel cells), rocket propellant (liquid hydrogen), laboratory reagent, semiconductor manufacturing, medical imaging (MRI contrast agents). |

These values give a comprehensive snapshot of hydrogen’s physical, chemical, and spectroscopic characteristics.
